Name: Meshach
Summary: Meshach was the Babylonian name given to Mishael, one of Daniel's three companions; he was set over the affairs of the province of Babylon and, with Shadrach and Abednego, refused the golden image and survived the fiery furnace. ONE profile covers both names; he is a different man from Mishael, son of Uzziel, who already has a profile.
KeyStory: Meshach stood with Shadrach and Abednego before the furnace and answered the king: our God is able to deliver us, but if not, we will not worship your image.
LifeLesson: 'But if not' is the deepest confession of faith — obedience that does not bargain for rescue.
RelatedEvents: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego in the Fiery Furnace
